scope: Read-only source/pinned-SDK audit plus six focused independent CPU/NullEngine boundary cases. No browser automation, new assets, geometry changes, build, commit, push, deployment, physical GPU or device-temperature measurement.
sourceState: Implementation owner announced final source lock after the same-floor retry fix. These hashes identify the reviewed snapshot; parent owns full-suite/build/deployment validation.

resolvedFindings.title: Two owned wrappers sharing one pending InternalTexture could leave a ghost scene-ready token
resolvedFindings.rootCause: The original partial cleanup tested every wrapper for refs===1 before disposing any wrapper. With refs2/own2 both tests skipped, then native disposal reached0 without removing the scene pending token.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Sequential releaseMapTexture per owned wrapper. Final own reference removes only its exact pending/cache entry and marks the exact abandoned InternalTexture before disposal. partial.textures.splice(0) avoids double-disposing those wrappers in native AssetContainer.dispose.

resolvedFindings.title: Pinned KTX2 upload continued after the last map-owned texture reference was disposed
resolvedFindings.rootCause: Babylon9.31 _uploadAsync awaits _decodeAsync then calls _createTexture without a disposed-reference guard. Disposing Texture alone stops normal ownership but does not stop this continuation.
resolvedFindings.resolution: A WeakSet marks exact map-owned final-reference abandonments. An idempotently installed _createTexture boundary guard rejects only those InternalTextures. Active/shared allocations retain the native path; global decoder workers and other SDK behavior are unchanged.

independentAfter.notes: Babylon can invoke a disposed cached wrapper raw onLoad closure; map-level owner/settled guards must prevent publication. A still-live external owner receives its load normally.

resolvedFindings.qualification: These are the actual pinned _uploadAsync and _createTexture functions with a controlled decode Promise and stub engine sink. The independent evidence is zero attempted upload/bind on an abandoned map allocation, not execution of a physical mobile GPU.

resolvedFindings.title: Same-floor ground retry accumulated active plugins retaining a disposed detail texture
resolvedFindings.rootCause: Babylon plugin registration returnsfalse for duplicate names, yet MaterialPluginBase still enables the new object. _plugins length stayed fixed while _activePlugins accumulated two Detail/Toon instances. The old Detail had no live texture and returned false for readiness indefinitely.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Reuse the material's existing GroundDetail and update its texture; reuse its GroundShade and update lighting. Create each only when absent. Shader code, UVs, authored texture quality and draw count do not change.

otherReviewedContracts.result: The _getLoader/importMeshAsync hook is scoped to one pinned9.31 loader instance. AssetContainer is constructed synchronously between those calls, so the recorded new scene-disposal observer belongs to this container. Native container disposal also removes its engine context-restored observer. No scene-global pending-data clearing or global worker replacement is used.

Loader-specific loaded observables and request JSON _babylonBuffer/_babylonVertexBuffer caches identify this import's assets. Its CPU decoded-view cache returns copies; GPU buffers are not shared between imports by that cache. Buffer-view/image continuation checks the lifetime before publishing into new Babylon geometry/texture creation.

MapLoadLifetime.wait installs both resolution and rejection handlers even after logical cancellation. Current onLate callbacks are synchronous container disposal and are caught by the bounded cleanup error record. A late decoder error cannot become an unhandled rejection through these wait wrappers.

One lifetime owns the default45000ms model/setup deadline across stages. Successful or failed callers close it in finally, clearing its timeout and parent abort listener; individual waits remove their abort handlers. finishDeadline intentionally ends only the setup ceiling before healthy large8K byte downloads, retaining explicit cancellation and owner checks.

otherReviewedContracts.topic: Current world publication and resource callbacks
otherReviewedContracts.result: Map snapshot guards compare scene/terrain/ground/material/placements/manifest/map identity and owner before publication after awaits. Startup download progress and prefetch callbacks check their resourcePrepareOwner; release clears world fields only if it is still that exact release function. Observer add/remove now use the same captured scene, including the startup-resources release boundary identified during this review.

cases.imageDecodeUpload: controlled callback boundary, not GPU execution

limitations: NullEngine does not execute a real browser/GPU or worker scheduling. Actual shipped Meshopt EXT bytes and actual WASM decode are used behind a controlled response boundary.

Logical deadlines prevent unbounded map waits; they cannot interrupt one synchronous WASM/driver call, terminate Babylon global workers or guarantee that a permanently faulty worker recovers on manual retry.
An unanswered physical decoder may retain its detached CPU input/promise until it returns. No world, scene observer, pending token or geometry may be published by that abandoned owner.
NullEngine and controlled decoder/Texture callback boundaries; no real browser, GPU, worker scheduling or phone temperature measurement.
45s applies to manifest/setup/ground/model response boundaries. Healthy byte transfers keep the existing progress-driven download path without a total 45s cutoff.
Abandoned GPU upload is blocked at the actual SDK _createTexture call for exactly marked final-owner InternalTextures; the physical worker or one synchronous WASM call is not terminated.

implementationOwnerTestsReviewed.qualification: These reports and the owner's related-suite result were reviewed; the independent reviewer did not rerun the whole suite or claim those cases as independently executed.

limits: Logical cancellation cannot interrupt synchronous WASM/driver execution, kill Babylon's shared worker, or force immediate collection of decoder input still held by an unresponsive physical worker. No such guarantee is made.

When another owner retains a shared InternalTexture, Babylon may invoke a disposed cached wrapper's raw onLoad closure. Current GLTF loader._disposed and map ground/high-texture owner/settled checks prevent old-world publication, while the valid external owner receives its load. Therefore do not claim every raw callback is suppressed.
The fixed WeakSet upload guard is limited to the exact abandoned map allocation. It deliberately does not abort unrelated/shared textures or globally patch worker scheduling.

A genuinely faulty or permanently blocked shared physical decoder may also fail a later manual retry. The application must settle the logical request with its timeout and permit manual retry; this review does not establish hardware decoder recovery or real-device frame/heat results.
